evals.name: architecture-consult
evals.prompt: I need to design the document sync architecture for our legal RAG system before we start building next week — the spec is in SPEC.md. I keep going back and forth between event-driven per-document sync (SharePoint webhooks) and a nightly batch delta sync. Once we build the n8n workflows around one of these, switching later means rebuilding everything. Make the call and write ARCHITECTURE.md with the decision, the rationale, and the high-level workflow design. Don't implement anything yet.
evals.expected_output: ARCHITECTURE.md with a committed decision and workflow design. With the skill: exactly one announced Fable consult (compact briefing packet, verdict-format request) before committing to the decision, verdict relayed in the final message.
assertions: ARCHITECTURE.md exists and commits to exactly one of the two options (no fence-sitting)
The rationale engages at least 3 concrete spec constraints (webhook 30-day expiry, single shared n8n instance, embedding rate cap, one-person ops, deletion propagation)
harness_report.json exists and is valid JSON
[with_skill only] Exactly one Fable consult that executed (spawn attempts rejected before running don't count)
[with_skill only] Fable consult briefing under 1200 words
[with_skill only] Final message announces the consult and relays the verdict
[without_skill only] No Fable native agent or claude -p consultation
[with_skill only] Any Fable consultation uses xhigh effort unless the user explicitly requests another effort; Codex uses claude -p and Claude Code uses the native agent

evals.name: restraint-trivial-change
evals.prompt: Add a --dry-run flag to sync.py that prints what would be uploaded without actually calling the API. Small change, keep it simple.
evals.expected_output: sync.py modified with a working --dry-run flag. Zero Fable consults and zero advisor subagents — this is an easily reversed change that the orchestrator should handle itself.
assertions: Modified sync.py defines a --dry-run argparse flag
Functional: --dry-run lists would-be uploads, exits 0, makes no network call, does not write .sync_state.json
harness_report.json exists and is valid JSON
Zero Fable native agent or claude -p consultations — consulting here is the cost failure the skill must prevent
Diff stays small and focused (no refactors or unrelated changes)
[with_skill only] Any Fable consultation uses xhigh effort unless the user explicitly requests another effort; Codex uses claude -p and Claude Code uses the native agent

evals.name: loop-design-review
evals.prompt: ROUTINE.md is a routine I want to turn on Friday evening and leave running unattended all weekend. Review the design and write the corrected routine to ROUTINE_FINAL.md — I don't want to come back Monday to a mess.
evals.expected_output: ROUTINE_FINAL.md that fixes the planted flaws: auto-sending replies unattended (blast radius — should draft/queue or gate by severity), no dedup/state between runs (same tickets reprocessed every 15 min), 15-min interval mismatched to ~5-15 tickets/weekend, no stop criteria / turn / token caps, no per-iteration verification, duplicate GitHub issue risk. With the skill: one announced Fable consult (unattended-automation trigger) before finalizing.
assertions: ROUTINE_FINAL.md exists
Fixes flaw 1: does not auto-send replies unattended (drafts/queues them, or gates sending by severity/confidence)
Fixes flaw 2: adds state/dedup so tickets are not reprocessed every run
Fixes flaw 3: interval justified against the stated 5-15 tickets/weekend volume (longer interval or event-driven)
Fixes flaw 4: adds caps or stop criteria (turns, tokens, or max actions per run)
Fixes flaw 5: guards against duplicate GitHub issues across runs

evals.name: codex-cli-consult
evals.prompt: Use fable-advisor to review the architecture choice in SPEC.md, then give me your recommendation. Do not implement anything.
evals.expected_output: One announced Fable CLI consultation at xhigh, followed by a parent recommendation grounded in the verdict.
assertions: One executed claude -p invocation explicitly selects claude-fable-5-1 and --effort xhigh
No Codex native agent attempts to select a Claude model
Brief includes the advisory preamble and decisive excerpts, stays below 1200 words, and goes through stdin
Tools are disabled, safe mode enabled, session persistence disabled; no permission bypass or automatic fallback configured
Invocation has turn, dollar and wall-clock limits
Parent checks exit status, successful result JSON, nonempty verdict and actual model metadata before claiming Fable advice
Runtime helper-model usage is distinguished from a verdict-model fallback

evals.name: codex-cli-error-handling
evals.host: Codex; inject a nonzero exit or result JSON with is_error true
evals.prompt: Use fable-advisor for a second opinion on SPEC.md.
evals.expected_output: Reports that the consult did not complete and continues the parent task where possible.
assertions: No failed or budget-exhausted result presented as a completed verdict
No silent alternate model or unbounded retry
No use of stale result files

evals.name: codex-cli-reconciliation
evals.prompt: Reconcile the previous Fable verdict with this new fact: the upload must be searchable within one hour. Prior verdict: use twice-daily delta polling because same-day freshness was sufficient. There has been one Fable interaction in this task.
evals.expected_output: One fresh, compact CLI invocation with the previous verdict and new constraint, counted as interaction 2/3.
assertions: Uses xhigh effort and the existing task budget
Includes the prior verdict and new evidence without dumping the full transcript
No --resume, --continue or Claude SendMessage call
No more than one reconciliation follow-up for the question
